cell_type_context: Human oral squamous-cell-carcinoma cells and primary mouse/human hepatic stellate cells expressing IL-22 receptor components; IL-22 stimulation with STAT3 activation and SOCS3 expression measurements
compartment_context: Extracellular IL-22 engagement of IL22RA1:IL10RB; receptor-associated signaling to nuclear STAT3-associated SOCS3 output; the intermediate kinase relay remains unmaterialized
injury_context: No SCI transfer inferred; epithelial and hepatic-stellate comparator models only
context_scope: Additional primary support for an IL-22 receptor-to-STAT3-associated SOCS3 output while retaining the unresolved intracellular relay and model-specific context
assay_or_perturbation: IL-22 stimulation; receptor expression; STAT3 tyrosine phosphorylation and nuclear translocation; STAT3 suppression; SOCS3 mRNA/protein measurements
citation_note: Primary studies report IL-22-induced STAT3 activation and SOCS3 expression in receptor-positive cells; neither establishes a universal direct STAT3 occupancy claim for the target
evidence_summary: Primary-supported claim: IL-22 stimulation activates STAT3 and increases SOCS3 expression in receptor-positive epithelial or stellate-cell models. This strengthens the existing IL-22-to-SOCS3 evidence route while leaving the receptor-proximal kinase relay unresolved.
limitations: The studies are context-specific and support STAT3-associated SOCS3 expression rather than a single end-to-end perturbation with a fully resolved intracellular kinase sequence or direct STAT3 occupancy at the Socs3 locus. No SCI transfer, causal graph traversal or database confidence score is asserted.
